API Reference

REST API Endpoints

The ClaudeScrap project provides a FastAPI-based REST API for remote scraping operations.

Authentication

All API endpoints require JWT authentication. Include the token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <your-jwt-token>

Endpoints

FastAPI endpoints for scraping service

api.scraping_api.verify_token(credentials=fastapi.Depends)[source]

Verify JWT token and extract user ID.

Validates the provided JWT token using the configured secret key and extracts the user identifier from the token payload.

Parameters:

credentials (HTTPAuthorizationCredentials) – Bearer token from request header

Returns:

User ID extracted from token subject claim

Return type:

str

Raises:

HTTPException – 401 status if token is invalid, expired, or malformed

Example

>>> # In request header: Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token>
>>> user_id = verify_token(credentials)
>>> print(f"Authenticated user: {user_id}")

Note

Uses HS256 algorithm for token validation. Token must contain ‘sub’ (subject) claim with user identifier.

async api.scraping_api.start_scraping(request, user_id=fastapi.Depends)

Start a new scraping job.

Initiates an asynchronous scraping job for the specified site and query. The job runs in the background and can be monitored via status endpoints.

Parameters:

  • request (ScrapingRequest) – Scraping configuration including site, query, and max_pages

  • user_id (str) – Authenticated user ID from JWT token

Returns:

Job details including unique job_id and status

Return type:

ScrapingResponse

Raises:

HTTPException – 401 for authentication errors, 500 for service errors

Example

>>> # POST /api/scraping/start
>>> # Body: {"site": "tokopedia", "query": "laptop", "max_pages": 5}
>>> # Response: {"job_id": "job_123", "status": "started", ...}

Note

Requires valid JWT token in Authorization header. Job execution is asynchronous and non-blocking.

async api.scraping_api.get_job_status(job_id, user_id=fastapi.Depends)

Get scraping job status and progress information.

Retrieves detailed status information for a specific scraping job including progress metrics and current state.

Parameters:

  • job_id (str) – Unique identifier of the scraping job

  • user_id (str) – Authenticated user ID from JWT token

Returns:

Job status information including:

  • job_id: Job identifier

  • status: Current status (running, completed, failed)

  • current_page: Current page being processed

  • total_pages: Total pages to process

  • products_found: Number of products extracted

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

Raises:

HTTPException – 404 if job not found, 401 for authentication errors

Example

>>> # GET /api/scraping/status/job_123
>>> # Response: {"job_id": "job_123", "status": "running", "current_page": 3, ...}

Note

Returns real-time progress information for active jobs.

async api.scraping_api.stop_scraping_job(job_id, user_id=fastapi.Depends)

Stop a running scraping job.

Gracefully terminates an active scraping job and releases associated resources.

Parameters:

  • job_id (str) – Unique identifier of the job to stop

  • user_id (str) – Authenticated user ID from JWT token

Returns:

Operation result with job_id, status, and message

Return type:

Dict[str, str]

Raises:

HTTPException – 404 if job not found, 500 for service errors

Example

>>> # POST /api/scraping/stop/job_123
>>> # Response: {"job_id": "job_123", "status": "stopped", "message": "..."}

Note

Stopping a job may take a few seconds to complete gracefully. Already completed jobs cannot be stopped.

async api.scraping_api.list_jobs(user_id=fastapi.Depends)

List all scraping jobs for the authenticated user.

Retrieves a comprehensive list of all scraping jobs associated with the authenticated user, including their current status.

Parameters:

user_id (str) – Authenticated user ID from JWT token

Returns:

Dictionary containing ‘jobs’ key with list of job objects

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

Example

>>> # GET /api/scraping/jobs
>>> # Response: {
>>> #   "jobs": [
>>> #     {"job_id": "job_1", "status": "completed", "site": "tokopedia", ...},
>>> #     {"job_id": "job_2", "status": "running", "site": "shopee", ...}
>>> #   ]
>>> # }

Note

Returns jobs in reverse chronological order (newest first).

async api.scraping_api.health_check()

Health check endpoint for service monitoring.

Provides a simple health status check for monitoring systems and load balancers to verify service availability.

Returns:

Health status with service identifier

Return type:

Dict[str, str]

Example

>>> # GET /health
>>> # Response: {"status": "healthy", "service": "scraping-api"}

Note

Does not require authentication. Used by monitoring systems to verify service health.
